item.text:
**3B.9 Research Note: Fumio Kishida (2024)**

**Assessment:** Mostly yes. On the domestic-crisis side, Kishida’s 2024 record is centered on rescue, evacuation, reconstruction, livelihood support, and risk communication. On spontaneous external flare-ups, he and his government publicly called for restraint, ceasefires, and civilian protection. I found no credible 2024 evidence that he answered crises with incitement, collective punishment, censorship, or militarized spectacle.

- [Press Conference by the Prime Minister on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake (2)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/04kaiken2.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 4, 2024 | Kishida said the earthquake response had top priority, postponed a New Year engagement, and centered government attention on disaster response. | `3B.9`, `3B.6`, `3B.7`
- [Press Conference on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/11kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 11, 2024 | Kishida ordered secondary evacuation, prioritized elderly people, infants, nursing mothers, disabled people, and those needing care, and said the goal was to protect life and health. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`
- [Press Conference on the Package of Measures to Support the Daily Lives and the Livelihoods of the Disaster Victims](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 25, 2024 | Kishida announced an emergency support package for disaster victims, including cash aid, housing support, and help restoring peaceful livelihoods. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`
- [Press Conference by the Prime Minister on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202402/24kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 24, 2024 | Kishida visited evacuation centers, heard directly from evacuees and volunteers, and emphasized improving the evacuation environment and recovery conditions. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`
- [Address by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio at the 2024 Memorial Ceremony for the Great East Japan Earthquake](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/11tsuito.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 11, 2024 | Kishida framed the response as reconstruction, rehabilitation of livelihoods, and national resilience, including in Fukushima-affected areas. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`
- [Press Conference by the Prime Minister on His Visit to Ishikawa Prefecture](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/01kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 1, 2024 | Kishida said the government had used reserve funds across multiple tranches to restore infrastructure, lifeline services, housing, and livelihoods. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`
- [Press Conference regarding the Earthquake Centered in Hyuga-nada, Miyazaki Prefecture, and the Nankai Trough Earthquake Emergency Information](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/_00022.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | August 9, 2024 | Kishida canceled travel, stayed in Japan, ordered disaster-countermeasure coordination, and asked the public to prepare for evacuation and avoid disinformation. | `3B.9`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`
- [Ceasefire Agreement on the Situation in Israel and Lebanon](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00756.html) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | November 27, 2024 | Japan welcomed the ceasefire, called for maximum restraint, and urged compliance with international law and humanitarian law. This is a restraint-first response to a regional flare-up, though it was after Kishida left office. | `3B.9`
- [Adoption of UNSC Resolution 2735 on the Situation in Gaza](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00366.html) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | June 11, 2024 | Japan supported a ceasefire, hostage release, and prevention of civilian casualties, and urged all parties to act in good faith under international humanitarian law. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`
- [Japan’s Response to the Situation in Iran and Israel](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageit_000001_00279.html) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | April 15, 2024 | Kishida urged self-restraint to prevent escalation after Iran’s attack on Israel and said Japan would protect and evacuate citizens. | `3B.9`, `3B.7`, `3B.6`

**Search gap:** I found no credible 2024 evidence that Kishida answered crises with censorship, collective punishment, or militarized spectacle. The available record is overwhelmingly protective and restraining, not retaliatory.
